statusText: CME equity futures are halted for twelve of the twenty-four published hours, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue, and no U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the window. Three items advanced the evidence ledger this run without changing its balance: an IRGC strike on a Togo-flagged tanker inside the Strait of Hormuz, an Iranian fire pause that has now run ten days, and an Aramco export ramp through the same strait.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 18, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: A Hormuz interdiction enters the ledger against a ten-day Iranian fire pause and a rising Aramco export run through the same strait: every primary mark re-verifies unchanged, and a two-sided weekend still points to two-way discovery at the 22:00Z restart
body:
Twelve of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final twelve contain the 22:00Z restart, the hours after it and the Asian and early European sessions that follow. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run and every one is unchanged: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44 inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. Crude settled easier for a third consecutive session, WTI at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, although WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month because the East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike.

Three items advanced the evidence ledger this run, and they do not all point the same way. First, and newly entering this assessment, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy says it struck a Togo-flagged tanker inside the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, stating that the vessel came to a halt after catching fire during what Tehran described as an illegal passage; reporting identifies the vessel as the Trend and says it was detained, while UKMTO logged a separate unidentified incident in the same area. That is a direct interdiction inside the transmission channel this assessment watches most closely, and it is the first such item in the current ledger. Second, and cutting the other way, an Iran war chronology dated 18 September records that the Iranian fire pause reached a tenth consecutive day through 19 September, with no ballistic salvo at any of the six Arabian Peninsula Gulf states, Jordan or Israel since the 8-9 September launches. Third, Reuters-sourced reporting confirms Saudi Aramco has sold around 60 million barrels for September and October loading via ship-to-ship transfer in Oman, lifting exports from inside the Gulf to an average of 1.0-1.5 million barrels per day, with Chinese, South Korean, Indian and Japanese refiners the main buyers, and notes that Riyadh may partially restore the East-West pipeline. An interdiction against a fire pause and a rising export run through the same strait is a wider distribution, not a directional one.

A fourth item is a dated policy checkpoint rather than a market input. Trump told Axios on 17 September that he faces a decision on whether to resume large-scale attacks on Iran, and reporting places a meeting with the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman on 22 September at the UN General Assembly in New York. No exact time is published for that meeting, so under the calendar contract used here it is omitted from the published events array and carried only as a named checkpoint. It falls outside the 24 hours published in this assessment.

The rest of the ledger stands as before and was re-verified. Saudi authorities confirm that the ballistic missile attempt on Riyadh was accompanied by attacks on Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan and state that all of them were intercepted or thwarted, with no casualties and no damage reported and Aramco declining to comment on the Houthi claim of massive fires. The State Department alerts issued on Saturday evening covering Israel, Lebanon, Jordan, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE and Oman remain in force, warning that the conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly and flagging possible flight cancellations and airspace closures. On the repairing side, Hormuz throughput remains elevated, with satellite data showing Saudi movements of about 2.8 million barrels per day against roughly 700,000 in August.

The macro backdrop is restrictive and unchanged. The FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, and sixteen of eighteen participants expect at least one further increase this year. The H.15 release dated 18 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. That backdrop is the persistent named driver carried across the published hours, and a yield extension during Asian trade is the cross-asset condition most likely to slow the Tail decay published after the restart.

Two index-level checkpoints sit just outside the window. The Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance is confirmed and takes effect at Monday's cash open, lifting SpaceX from a weight of about 1.28% to 2.82% on Friday's closing prices; more than 200 products tracking the benchmark, with over $800bn in assets including the Invesco QQQ Trust, must adjust. Separately, a US-China meeting has been reported for the coming week but is not confirmed by Beijing, so it is likewise omitted from the published calendar. Mechanical rebalancing turnover is not the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures.

Friday's tape supports carrying no structural amplifier forward. The session was rotational rather than uniform - the Nasdaq added 0.7% while the Dow closed about 95 points lower and the S&P 500 rose 0.2%. Latest-session internals corroborate that split: four of the eight Nasdaq megacaps closed higher and four lower, with a mean change near +0.24%, while semiconductors led at roughly +1.28% mean, with QCOM an outlier at -5.82%, and both software industry groups closed lower. That shared context is delayed latest-session data and is used here only as confirmation, never as live NQ price evidence; this run it was collected outside its freshness window and its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so it carries less weight than in earlier runs and independent research was performed in full.

Current Tail stays at the closed-venue floor of 5: no venue is open and no structure has been observed. Stress moves one point to 31, because the Hormuz interdiction is a genuine addition to the escalation side of the ledger while the ten-day fire pause and the rising export run are genuine additions to the repairing side, leaving only a small net widening of the conditional distribution. Confidence rises one point to 75: three independently verified new items, a fully re-verified seven-day calendar and unchanged primary marks outweigh one more hour of distance from the Friday tape and a stale, partial shared-context file. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday; the China loan prime rate decision has already resolved, held at 3.00% and 3.50% for a sixteenth month, matching all 21 forecasts in the Reuters survey. The first Monday catalyst, the Goolsbee remarks at 10:30Z, sits just beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail is published at 5 through the early halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, reaching a window high of 18 at the restart before easing through the Asian session. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first twelve slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final five slots. Stress opened at 22, drifted through 23 and 24 across the Saturday afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 shortly after midnight, eased to 25 and then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation headlines landed, easing to 28 and then holding 30 across the final three slots. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence started at 76, decayed to a 72 trough at 21:00Z as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Twelve of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final twelve contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian and European hours after it. Cash closed Friday 18 September and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, just beyond its end, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for the current hour, then steps through 6, 7 and 8 across the European Sunday afternoon before advancing one point per hour to a pre-restart 15 at 21:00Z. It reaches the window high of 18 at the 22:00Z restart, eases to 17 for the first full hour and then decays through 15, 14, 13, 12 and 11 before flattening at 10 for the final five hours. That drift tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure and stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping in every published hour. Mode is published as event/whipsaw for the restart and the hour after it, then mixed for the first three Asian hours, reflecting expected two-way discovery against a weekend that produced a Hormuz interdiction, a ten-day Iranian fire pause and a rising Aramco export run at the same time; it returns to normal for the final seven hours on the base case that repricing has cleared. The Nasdaq-100 rebalance effective at Monday's cash open and the reported 22 September Trump meeting with Gulf leaders both sit beyond the window and are carried as checkpoints, not amplifiers.
